LESSON: ENERGY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Human and Economic Activities
Topic 3.3: Energy
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Energy, part of Human and Economic Activities in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is renewable energy important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Energy together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The skill of open-mindedness is enhanced as the learner develops energy-saving

devices using locally available materials.

● Learning to Learn: The skill of carrying out research is developed as the learner carries out a field study on energy within

the locality.

● Citizenship: The skill of global awareness is promoted as the learner watches/listen to audio-visual clips on development of

renewable energy in Kenya and the selected countries.

Values:
● Unity: Learner cooperates as they carry out field study on energy within the locality and write a report.

● Responsibility: Learner takes safety precautions as they make energy-saving devices using locally available materials and

showcase in the school.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

● Environmental Education: Learner participates in writing an article on the effects of mining on environment and possible
